# Palisade policy document

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask docs generate` from `schemas/policy/v1.json`. Do not edit by hand. -->

A versioned policy document: one policy and the rule sets it uses.

Schema: [`schemas/policy/v1.json`](https://github.com/jusso-dev/palisade/blob/main/schemas/policy/v1.json) (`$id` `https://github.com/jusso-dev/palisade/schemas/policy/v1.json`), version 1.0.0. Regenerate the schema with `PALISADE_BLESS=1 cargo test -p palisade-policy --test schema`, then these pages with `cargo xtask docs generate`.

## Object types

- [`Action`](action.md): The action of a rule (#34).
- [`ClientFilter`](client-filter.md): The client connected to a remote desktop session, for per-client scoping on multi-session hosts. Each list that is set must match.
- [`CloudObject`](cloud-object.md): An object in a cloud directory: a group of users or of devices.
- [`Criterion`](criterion.md): A test of one fact about the object or its context: `field operator values`.
- [`DateRange`](date-range.md): An inclusive range of dates. `to` unset means the single day `from`.
- [`DeviceRef`](device-ref.md): A device or group of devices (#38).
- [`DirectoryGroup`](directory-group.md): A directory group.
- [`Effects`](effects.md): The effect flags of one rule. Unset fields take the action's default.
- [`LibraryRef`](library-ref.md): A reference to a library from a match tree or a hierarchy assignment.
- [`LocationProfile`](location-profile.md): A named network location, such as `corporate`: every test must match (#38). The agent evaluates the profiles when the network changes and on every heartbeat, and scopes test the result with `location_profile`.
- [`Match`](match.md): A condition tree (#33).
- [`Metadata`](metadata.md): Governance metadata (#40). More fields arrive with #40.
- [`ModeOptions`](mode-options.md): Mode settings besides the base `mode`. Each is optional in a document.
- [`NetworkRef`](network-ref.md): A network location test (#38). Address tests match when any local interface address does.
- [`OuRef`](ou-ref.md): A directory organisational unit.
- [`Policy`](policy.md): The decision part of a policy: which rule sets apply, and how.
- [`PolicySettings`](policy-settings.md): Settings that apply to the whole policy. Every field is optional in a document and has the default shown in the schema.
- [`PrecedenceOptions`](precedence-options.md): Settings of the precedence models. Each is optional in a document.
- [`PrincipalRef`](principal-ref.md): A user or group (#38). Each is an object with one key, the kind.
- [`PromptSettings`](prompt-settings.md): How the `prompt` level asks the user.
- [`RefList`](ref-list.md): An `include` and an `exclude` list. An empty `include` means every entry; a match in `exclude` always wins.
- [`RefList2`](ref-list2.md): An `include` and an `exclude` list. An empty `include` means every entry; a match in `exclude` always wins.
- [`RefList3`](ref-list3.md): An `include` and an `exclude` list. An empty `include` means every entry; a match in `exclude` always wins.
- [`Rule`](rule.md): One rule: a match tree and the action taken when it matches.
- [`RuleSet`](rule-set.md): A named, reusable, ordered collection of rules.
- [`RuleSetScope`](rule-set-scope.md): The scopes of one rule-set assignment: every one must match for the set's rules to apply.
- [`Schedule`](schedule.md): When a scope is active (#38).
- [`Scope`](scope.md): Who, where and when a rule applies (#38).
- [`ScopeLimit`](scope-limit.md): One contributing policy's limit on where its unknown settings apply, in an effective policy (`UnknownPolicy::scope_limits`). It holds when every scope of `all_of` matches and, if `any_of` is not empty, one of its scopes matches.
- [`SessionFilter`](session-filter.md): Session criteria (#38).
- [`UnknownPolicy`](unknown-policy.md): The unknown-application policy (#39). Every field is optional in a document; the defaults block every unknown object.
- [`Window`](window.md): One weekly window.

Enumerations and string formats: [Value types](types.md).

## Examples

Each example passes this schema and full validation (`cargo test -p palisade-policy --test yaml`, in CI).

- [`actions-and-effects.yaml`](../../../../../examples/policies/actions-and-effects.yaml): Rule actions and effect flags (#34). Each rule set kind holds the actions it is for; a `mixed` set holds any. Effect flags are optional: an unset flag takes the action's default (see the palisade-policy README).
- [`context-criteria.yaml`](../../../../../examples/policies/context-criteria.yaml): Context criteria narrow an identity: who runs the object, where and when (#32, #33). Every rule still names the object by a hash, signer or path; the context only narrows it.
- [`finance-workstations.yaml`](../../../../../examples/policies/finance-workstations.yaml): Finance workstations: allow one line-of-business suite by publisher, product and minimum version, and keep PowerShell in audit while scripts are reviewed. `signer.publisher` is the signer's common name (the `CN` of the leaf certificate's subject), not the whole distinguished name.
- [`first-match.yaml`](../../../../../examples/policies/first-match.yaml): A firewall-style policy: rules are ordered, and the first rule that matches and does not defer decides (#35). Curated rule sets come first (curated_first, the default). The mandatory blocklist is checked before every ordered rule, whatever its order.
- [`minimal.yaml`](../../../../../examples/policies/minimal.yaml): The smallest valid policy: no rule sets, so nothing is allowed and every file is reported (audit mode) by the implicit deny.
- [`scoped-rules.yaml`](../../../../../examples/policies/scoped-rules.yaml): Rule scoping: who, where and when a rule applies. Scopes narrow a rule; they never identify the object, which is the match tree's job, and they never widen a rule. A rule applies only when the policy's scope, its rule set's assignment scopes and its own scope all match.
- [`staged-rollout.yaml`](../../../../../examples/policies/staged-rollout.yaml): A staged rollout (#36): the policy is in audit, so what it would block is reported but runs. Executables are already enforced, a disconnected device enforces everything, and a new blocklist is tried in monitor mode. The mandatory blocklist blocks in every mode, and one deny rule is enforced in audit too (`always_enforce`).
- [`unknown-applications.yaml`](../../../../../examples/policies/unknown-applications.yaml): Unknown-application handling (#39), starting from the Essential Eight maturity level 1 preset: unknown objects in user profiles, temporary folders and other user-writable locations are blocked, and elsewhere they are detected.
- [`workstation-baseline.yaml`](../../../../../examples/policies/workstation-baseline.yaml): A workstation baseline with hash, publisher and path rules (ISM-0955). The same document as tests/fixtures/valid/workstation-baseline.json.
